newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar hovers at lows as premium sold.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar hovers at lows as premium sold.

text.p: White sugar futures saw another day of solid turnover on Friday but price movements were subdued as the market consolidated after sharp declines earlier in the week.
Much of the activity came from against actuals and crossed trades and the nearby March/May spread remained in a slight contango.
The March arbitrage set the tone of the London market after the New York open as the premium narrowed from $71 to $70.
"It's come back in line with New York -- as the raws have come off, the whites have been offered down with it," said one trader.
The March/May spread also attracted steady trading interest but was trapped between buyers at 50 cents and sellers at flat, he said.
At 1711 GMT March was 50 cents lower at an intraday low of $295.40 but the day's range was tight at just $1.60. May was 60 cents higher at $296.50 and volume reached 2,149 lots.

March tumbled to a trough of $293.30 this week as bearish sentiment on the raws market -- sparked by a continued wave of fund liquidation -- kept London under pressure and widened the premium to around $71.
The low whites prices have also lured physical buyers, with Iraq, Iran, Indonesia and Pakistan cited as potential if not actual buyers this week.
But analysts said more physical offtake would be needed if prices were to regain some of the ground lost last week in a slide sparked by fund liquidation in the New York raws market.
"If the lower prices do not attract greater physical demand, the market is likely to remain in the doldrums," said statistician F.O. Licht in its Friday report.
Traders noted the start of a decline in open interest on March as the contract appraoches its expiry on February 13.
But the hefty volume of against actuals trades against the March contract last week indicated that the usual pre-expiry squeeze on holders of short positions was unlikely.
"I don't really see that there are going to be that many fireworks on March," said another trader.
Paris futures clawed their way higher in a much lighter volume of 618 lots.
March was up 40 cents at $295.80 and May up $1.30 at $297.00.
In other news, Colombian truckers demanding standby payments for time lost during a nine-day dockworkers' strike in Buenaventura prevented work from returning to normal on Friday.
The dockworkers returned to work on Friday morning, a day after winning a deal with shipowners and cargo handling operators that should more than double their wages.
